name: Bateham's mills and yard, Canal Street south of Harrison

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 716-719); when they were built is not known.

change_note: Built T-3831 (2026-11-28): Bateham's mills and yard in place of the context city's generic blocks on Canal Street.

placement.position_note: The main mill fronts the west walk of Canal Street (Andreas: the fire-plug 'in front of the mill, on Canal street, south of Harrison'), its south end eleven feet north of the Roelle building on Mather Street; the west mill eighty feet west of it. The block bounded by Harrison, Mather, Canal and Clinton streets (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718): Bateham's mills on Canal Street, the church on the north-east corner of Clinton and Mather, the Roelle building on Mather, the Huntoon place in the north-west quarter. The footprint's origin is local E -196.4 N -1512.4; the frame is turned onto the 1871 plan's grid.
placement.symbolic_location: Canal Street, west side, south of Harrison Street: the east half of the block bounded by Harrison, Mather, Canal and Clinton.

footprint.note: The mills' ground, 54.9 by 108 m (1.47 acres) against Andreas's 'one and a half acres': the two mills' widths and the eighty feet between them across, the mills' 245-foot length and the yard north of them along Canal.

blocks.name: the main mill
blocks.note: 'Bateham's three-story-and-attic mill. The building was two hundred and forty-five by sixty in size', on Canal Street, the fire-plug 'in front of the mill' (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718); 'large wooden structures, surrounded by combustible materials' (p. 716). Its windows, doors and storey heights are reconstructed; the attic is the roof's.

blocks.name: the west mill
blocks.note: 'Eighty feet west of the main mill was another of the same length, and forty feet in width' (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718). Its storeys and openings are reconstructed.

blocks.name: the engine and boiler house
blocks.note: The mill ran on steam: Bateham and his watchman 'at once started the steam engine, attaching the force-pump' (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718). Where its engine and boilers stood, and their house, are reconstructed: a brick boiler house against the main mill's west wall.

blocks.name: a kindling pile
blocks.note: 'A thousand cords of fire-kindling wood, in piles twenty-five feet high' in the yard (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718). The piles' number, sizes and places between the mills are reconstructed to that quantity.

value.note: BATEHAM'S MILLS, built by T-3831: William B. Bateham's planing and shingle mills and their yard on Canal Street.

fire.note: 'At half-past ten the heroic men were driven from Bateham's works by the intense heat' (Andreas p. 718).

composition.note: Sizes, storeys and the yard's contents from Andreas's account (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718); openings, the boiler house and stack, and where the piles stood are reconstructed.

wall_material.value: Sawn boards on a frame, shingle roofs; a brick boiler house
wall_material.note: 'Large wooden structures' (Andreas p. 716); the boards and shingles are reconstructed in kind.

function.note: William B. Bateham's planing mills, with a yard of kindling wood, furniture lumber and shingles (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718).

built.note: Not known: reconstructed as standing through the later 1860s.

research_note: BATEHAM'S MILLS, built by T-3831 for the 1871 scene: William B. Bateham's 'three-story-and-attic mill', 245 by 60 feet, on Canal Street south of Harrison, with a second mill of the same length and forty feet wide eighty feet west of it; a yard holding 'a thousand cords of fire-kindling wood, in piles twenty-five feet high', six hundred thousand feet of the Frank Mayer Furniture Company's lumber (the company had the mill's attic) and 750,000 shingles; the grounds an acre and a half (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 717-718). Bateham, an alderman, fought for his works with his own steam pump and the engines; at half-past ten the men were driven out by the heat, and he turned away: 'The materials from this mill will fire the South Side, and nothing can prevent it now.' No picture of the mills is known.
